title: Paul Gayten's Sizzling Six, Crystal Palace and WJDX broadcasts
summary: He plays matinees with Paul Gayten's small group at the Crystal Palace and Savoy, broadcasts on WJDX, and hears visiting big bands.

bands.name: Paul Gayten and His Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was 14 when I joined that band. And then Paul Gayten put another little group together called Paul Gayten and His Sizzling Six. We had two saxophones. There was Duke Holliston, and Duke was playing tenor with this group. And we had a guitar player, a fine guitar player, who made some marks later on down in Detroit, named Emmett Slade. And we had Paul on piano and Mark Hannah(?) on the drums. And if I remember correctly, there was a boy named Leon Spann who had come up from Piney Woods, Mississippi, with a band down there; e had worked with the Don Dunbar band; he replaced Doug(?)/Dump(?)/Doc(?) Harvey. And he later ...(?)...(?)... played with the Freddie Johnston Orchestra.
So we had this little thing. We would play matinees every Monday at the ballrooms... The Crystal Palace was the first one that we played. Our first gig was at the Crystal Palace Ballroom...

Yeah. It was on North Farris Street in Jackson. That was the big dance hall where all the bands played. I had an opportunity to hear a lot of great bands, like Earl Hines, Tiny Bradshaw, (?), they had Joe Robicheaux -- a lot of different bands that came through there. I heard Andy Kirk's band, and also Erskine Hawkins. And we also had another ballroom called the Savoy Ballroom, and I used to play there on some matinees that they would have at the Savoy with Paul Gayten's little group. And we also used to broadcast on radio station WJDX in Jackson, which was a big deal. You know, every Saturday we'd broadcast...! [LAUGHS] And we were pretty hot stuff around at that time...
Round about 1938. Yeah, around 1938, '39, like that. I was getting a good start, a good start.
